episodes.153870: Ahead of an advancing cold front, an isolated rotating thunderstorm prompted a Tornado Warning for eastern Martha's Vineyard and a portion of Cape Cod.  Although no tornado occurred, there were severe wind gusts on Cape Cod.
episodes.154312: A brief period of severe thunderstorm winds and flooding occurred over the Marianas.
episodes.154450: A southeasterly flow brought deep tropical moisture into the area, producing periods of moderate to heavy showers across southern PR.

events.narrative: Morning scatterometer data depicted a surface trough just to the east of the Marianas. Upper-level analysis also showed an upper low and trough just to the west of the islands. ||The combination of the two casued an area of scattered to numerous showers and|isolated thunderstorms to develop on the trough east of the islands. The scatterometer data did depict higher winds associated with the trough near Tinian and Saipan. By 449 local time winds gusted to 29 knots (33 mph) at the Saipan airport. Gusty winds in the upper 20 to mid 30 knot range persisted across Saipan until 1000 local time with a gust to 36 knots (41mph) at 955. ||Further south the thunderstorms along the trough collapsed and produced a outflow |boundary. This boundary headed west towards Guam. While winds were also gusty across Guam just before noon, the outflow boundary produced strong wind gusts at a few locations over the island. Andersen AFB saw a wind gust to 44 knots (51mph) at 154 local time and at the National Weather Service Office the highest wind gust was 49 knots (56 mph) a 1202. ||The winds caused some damage to trees on Guam. Power outages did occur in a areas over Guam and was reported in Yigo, Dededo, and Yona.

As an outflow boundary generated from collapsing thunderstorms east of Guam passed over the island low-level convergence produced an area of brief heavy showers and thunderstorms, mainly over the southwest section of the island. |Rainfall varied over much of the island with 24 hour amounts at the National Weather |Service Office (Central Guam) totaling to 1.08 inches. Andersen AFB saw 2.23 inches |for the day. A USGS rain gage over the southwest section of the island (Alamagosa |Rain Gage near Santa Rita) recored 3.16 inches between 1145 and 1530. Another USGS Gage (Umatic) saw 2.40 inches between 1215 and 1500. A rain gage owned by a private individual (Casa Davis - ISANTA194) just south of Agat recorded 7.90 inches between 1124 and 1359 Guam time. This would equate to 3.06 inches per hour. The accuracy of the gage is uncertain, but it certainly indicates that rainfall was heavy for a short period of time.   |USGS stream gages saw a rapid rise of a few streams over the southern section of Guam.  A stream gage on the Ugum River above Talofofo Falls, rose from a stream height of 1.24 feet at 1150 to 9.98 feet at 1350 which is a 8.74 foot change. A USGS gage on the Imong River near Agat rose from a height of 9.42 feet at 1150 to 17.57 feet at 1305 which is an 8.15 foot change and a gage on the La Sa Fua River|near Umatac rose from a height of 10.8 feet at 1150 to 17.16 feet at 1305L a 6.36 foot change.||Flooding was observed in Umatic as the river in the village rose quickly. There was a report of a cow being washed out to sea (althogh video of the event seemed to show that the animal may have been a horse). Minor flooding was reported along Road PR-1 in Barrio Jauca. Additionally, a house was affected by the flooding.
In Hyannis, a mesonet site recorded a wind gust to 63 mph at 1150 AM EST.
In Dennis, a mesonet site recorded a wind gust to 61 mph at 1216 PM EST.
In Wellfleet, on Lieutenant Island, an amateur radio operator recorded a wind gust to 65 mph at 1219 PM EST.
